edition.locus: Gebhardt VII.XX (the cow; Sanavivaria; stand in faith)

source_text: Puellis autem ferocissimam uaccam, ideoque praeter consuetudinem comparatam, diabolus praeparauit, sexui earum etiam de bestia aemulatus. Itaque dispoliatae et reticulis indutae producebantur. Horruit populus alteram respiciens puellam delicatam, alteram a partu recentem stillantibus mammis. Ita reuocatae et discinctis indutae. Prior Perpetua iactata est, et concidit in lumbos. Et ubi sedit, tunicam a latere discissam ad uelamentum femoris reduxit, pudoris potius memor quam doloris. Dehinc acu requisita et dispersos capillos infibulauit. Non enim decebat martyram sparsis capillis pati, ne in sua gloria plangere uideretur. Ita surrexit, et elisam Felicitatem cum uidisset, accessit et manum ei tradidit et suscitauit illam. Et ambae pariter steterunt. Et populi duritia deuicta reuocatae sunt in portam Sanauiuariam. Illic Perpetua a quodam tunc catechumino, Rustico nomine, qui ei adhaerebat, suscepta et quasi a somno expergita (adeo in spiritu et in extasi fuerat) circumspicere coepit, et instupentibus omnibus ait: Quando, inquit, proiciemur ad uaccam illam nescio quam? Et cum audisset quod iam euenerat, non prius credidit nisi quasdam notas uexationis in corpore et habitu suo recognouisset. Exinde accersitum fratrem suum, et illum catechuminum, adlocuta est dicens: In fide state et inuicem omnes diligite, et passionibus nostris ne scandalizemini.
pass_a_gloss: For the girls the devil got ready a most fierce cow, obtained beyond custom, begrudging even their sex in respect of the beast. Stripped therefore and put into nets they were brought forth. The people shuddered looking at the one delicate girl, the other fresh from birth with breasts dripping. So they were called back and put into unbelted clothes. Perpetua first was thrown and fell on her loins. And when she sat she pulled the tunic torn at the side toward covering of thigh, remembering shame rather than pain. Then with a pin asked for she pinned up the scattered hairs. For it did not befit a martyr to suffer with loose hair, lest she be seen to lament in her glory. So she got up, and when she saw Felicity crushed she went and gave her hand and lifted her. And both stood together. And with the hardness of the people overcome they were recalled to the Sanavivarian Gate. There Perpetua, taken up by a certain then-catechumen Rusticus by name who was clinging to her, and as if roused from sleep (so far in spirit and in ecstasy she had been), began to look about, and with all astounded said: When, she says, shall we be thrown to that I-know-not-what cow? And when she heard that it had already happened, she did not believe before she recognized certain marks of the harassment on her body and dress. Then having summoned her brother and that catechumen she spoke saying: Stand in faith and love one another all, and do not be stumbled by our sufferings.
pass_b_english: For the young women, however, the devil prepared a most savage heifer, procured contrary to custom for this very reason, begrudging their sex even in the choice of the beast. Stripped therefore and clothed in nets they were led out. The crowd shuddered as it gazed upon the one, a delicate girl, the other fresh from childbirth with dripping breasts. So they were recalled and clothed in loose robes. Perpetua was tossed first, and fell upon her loins. And when she sat up, she drew the tunic torn from the side to make a covering for her thigh, mindful of modesty rather than of pain. Then she asked for a pin and fastened up her scattered hair. For it was not fitting for a martyr to suffer with loose hair, lest she seem to be mourning in her glory. So she rose, and when she saw Felicity crushed, she went to her and gave her her hand and raised her up. And both stood together.

And when the hardness of the crowd was overcome, they were recalled to the Sanavivarian Gate. There Perpetua, received by a certain man who was then a catechumen, Rusticus by name, who kept close to her, and as if awakened from sleep, for she had been so far in spirit and in ecstasy, began to look around, and while all stood amazed she said: When, she said, are we to be thrown to that heifer I know not what. And when she heard that it had already happened, she would not believe it until she recognized certain marks of the affliction on her body and on her dress. Thereupon she summoned her brother and that catechumen and addressed them, saying: Stand firm in the faith and love one another, all of you, and do not be made to stumble by our sufferings.

lemmas.gloss: heifer, cow let loose against the women
begrudging, envying with hostile intent here
nets put on them as covering
loins, lower back on which she fell
ecstasy, being outside oneself in spirit
be made to stumble, be scandalized

choices.why: discinctis is ablative plural of discinctus, unbelted, contrasting the nets; indutae requires a garment in ablative, so loose outer dress rather than nakedness
proper name of the arena gate where the living leave; kept as name rather than translating as Life Gate to preserve procedural sense

choices.english: do not be made to stumble
choices.why: passive subjunctive with passionibus as cause; moral stumbling, not mere offense, fits martyr exhortation

variants: dispersos capillos infibulauit: lacuna marker (*] lacuna, cf. Gr.) — the Greek carries the pin detail; kept as printed.
